I am a 57-year-old farmer in Quzhou with 8 mu of good irrigated land. I only finished primary school, but I have farmed here for more than 30 years and I know what works on my fields. Last October I planted winter wheat with improved seed — I stopped using the old traditional varieties years ago because my neighbor switched and his yield was much better. Now it is spring, the wheat is turning green, and I need to water and fertilize it. I thought about planting some cotton on a piece of land this year like a few people in my village do, but cotton needs too much pesticide and my wife and I are getting old — our backs cannot handle all that bending to pick cotton. I will stick with winter wheat and then summer maize on all 8 mu. This double cropping is safe. Even if the weather is bad for one crop, the other usually keeps us from losing everything.

For my wheat, I will irrigate three times: once now to wake it up, once at jointing, and once during grain filling. I use about 16 kg of nitrogen per mu total, putting some compound fertilizer down as a base and topdressing with urea when the wheat starts to joint. I also need phosphorus and potassium from the compound fertilizer. I will spray three times for weeds, insects, and rust if I see it. I rotary-tilled the land before sowing last autumn. If the weather is normal, I expect about 500 kg per mu.

After I harvest the wheat in early June, I will plant hybrid maize immediately. There is no time to waste — the growing season is tight — so I will use no-tillage and sow straight into the wheat stubble. The maize needs about 18 kg of nitrogen per mu, plus some compound fertilizer. I will irrigate twice and spray twice for weeds and bugs. I should get around 550 kg per mu of maize. I know fertilizer is expensive this year, but I cannot afford to under-apply and lose the crop. It is better to spend the money and make sure my family has enough to eat and some grain left to sell.
